- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.30) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% relative to model output.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; apply downward correction of 3–8% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., < -0.30) over last 5–7 days, model underestimates downward trend; add 2–5% to forecast to account for mean reversion.
- Model frequently underestimates long-term (15+ day) price movements; increase forecast by 1–3% for horizon >15 days if sentiment is neutral or positive.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive (e.g., +0.30+ in 2 consecutive days), model lags in adjusting; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days and apply +2–4% bias to catch momentum.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often underestimates final 5–7 days; add 1–3% to last 5–7 forecast values to align with observed mean reversion toward higher levels.
